extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and stakeholders who track or participate in FAR rulemaking (federal contractors, procurement policy staff, regulatory commenters)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and required elements for entries in the Semiannual Regulatory Agenda (FAR-related) and the accompanying Federal Register notice that summarize, track, and invite participation in FAR rulemaking activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal Status of FederalRegister.gov content
rubrics_metrics.description: This site displays a prototype of a “Web 2.0” version of the daily Federal Register. It is not an official legal edition of the Federal Register, and does not replace the official print version or the official electronic version on GPO’s govinfo.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents posted are XML renditions and each includes a link to the corresponding official PDF file on govinfo.gov. While efforts are made to ensure accuracy, those relying on it for legal research should verify against an official edition. Until ACFR grants official status, the XML rendition does not provide legal notice to the public or judicial notice to the courts. Only official editions provide legal notice under 44 U.S.C. 1503 & 1507.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Semiannual Regulatory Agenda
rubrics_metrics.description: This agenda provides summary descriptions of regulations being developed by the Civilian Agency Acquisition Council and the Defense Acquisition Regulations Council in compliance with Executive Orders (12866, 13563, 14192).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published to allow interested people an opportunity to participate in the rulemaking process and to allow public tracking of open and pending FAR rules (e.g., via the 'Open FAR Cases' report). The agenda attempts to list all regulations pending at publication except minor/routine/repetitive actions; omission of an item has no legal significance and dates shown are estimates, not commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document Headings / Required Sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Document headings vary by document type but may contain the following: AGENCY; ACTION; SUMMARY; FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT; SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These headings form internal navigation links; the table of contents is a navigational tool and the repetition of headings has no substantive legal effect. See the Document Drafting Handbook for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry elements for each Agenda item (Legal Authority, Abstract, Timetable, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each listed regulatory action contains entries such as Legal Authority; Abstract; Timetable; Regulatory Flexibility Analysis Required; Agency Contact; RIN (Regulation Identifier Number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timetable rows show actions (e.g., NPRM, NPRM Comment Period End, Final Rule, Interim Final Rule Effective) with Date and FR Cite where applicable. Include Agency Contact with name, address, phone, email. State whether a Regulatory Flexibility Analysis is required. Provide RIN and identifier number for tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timetable formatting and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Timetable entries list Action, Date, and FR Cite for stages of rulemaking (e.g., NPRM, Comment Period End, Final Rule, Interim Final Rule, Effective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates shown are estimated and are not commitments to act on or by the dates shown. Timetables may include multiple entries and extended/extended_end dates where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each rule entry includes an Abstract summarizing the rule's purpose, scope, and statutory or executive order basis (e.g., what the rule will require or do and under which authorities it is issued).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts may also note relationship to previous proposals, public comments received and under consideration, and policy context (e.g., Executive Orders or Acts driving the rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comments and regulations.gov linkage
rubrics_metrics.description: Published proposed rules may be reviewed in their entirety at the Government's rulemaking website at https://www.regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agenda indicates whether public comments were received and being considered. For this document, 'Comments are no longer being accepted' is shown; for other items, comment periods and their end dates are listed in the timetable. Provide links to dockets where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: For each item provide Agency Contact: name, office/position, mailing address, phone number, and email address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact details are used for further information and should be listed consistently for each action (e.g., 'William Clark, Director, Office of Government-wide Acquisition Policy...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Analysis indication
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry includes whether a Regulatory Flexibility Analysis is required (Yes/No).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit notation in the item header; this informs stakeholders about expected economic-analysis requirements under the Regulatory Flexibility Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifiers and citations (CFR, FR citation, Document Number, RIN)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries include CFR references (e.g., 48 CFR chapter I), Document Citation (e.g., 90 FR 45580), Document Number (e.g., 2025-18316), and RIN/regulation identifier numbers (e.g., 9000-AO49).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These identifiers enable precise tracking and retrieval. Provide them for each rule listed and include printed page numbers when available (e.g., printed page 45580).

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of official formats and public inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: This document and entries are available in multiple formats: PDF (official printed version on govinfo.gov), JSON (normalized attributes), XML (original full text XML), MODS (GPO metadata).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the PDF linked in the document sidebar for the official electronic format. Public Inspection copies and links should be provided and users advised to verify against final official editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice about omissions and non-binding dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulatory Secretariat Division has attempted to list all regulations pending at time of publication, except for minor and routine or repetitive actions; however, unanticipated requirements may result in issuance of regulations not included. There is no legal significance to the omission of an item from this listing. Also, the dates shown for steps of each action are estimated and not commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders should not rely on inclusion or specific dates as creating legal rights or obligations; check official sources for binding information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of rule stages / grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: The agenda groups FAR actions by stage (Proposed Rule Stage, Final Rule Stage, Completed Actions) and assigns sequence numbers and titles for each FAR Case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each grouped entry includes stage-appropriate elements (e.g., Proposed Rule Stage shows NPRM and comment period; Final Rule Stage shows final rule dates). Use grouping to understand status and next steps for each FAR case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of supporting references and handbooks
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice references supporting materials (e.g., the Document Drafting Handbook) for further details on document drafting and headings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and drafters should consult the Document Drafting Handbook and agency guidance for formatting, headings, and drafting conventions when preparing Federal Register entries.
